UnitStatement: This chapter treats Chirality agent instruction files, governance documents, and binding contracts as a coherent engineered system.
Chapter 3's four pillars are argued to motivate and organize the systems engineering disciplines present in Chirality.
Each examined systems engineering discipline is present in the architecture and traces to one or more philosophical pillars.
No examined systems engineering discipline is found that does not serve a philosophical pillar.
The systems engineering disciplines emerged as a coherent way to make the four-pillar commitments architecturally real in Chirality.
The INCOSE Systems Engineering Handbook is used as the reference framework for systems engineering discipline definitions.
The analysis method traces evidence to specific files, governance sections, and invariant identifiers from CONTRACT.md.
The epistemology pillar is served most densely by configuration management, verification and validation, formal methods, and the evidence-first epistemology pattern.
If epistemology is the load-bearing pillar, it should be the pillar served by the most systems engineering disciplines.
The analysis scope is limited to agent instruction files, governance documents, and invariant contracts.
The chapter analyzes eight disciplines: architecture, configuration management, verification and validation, safety, requirements, control theory, formal methods, and human factors.
Architecture and structural design concerns decomposition into subsystems with defined boundaries, interfaces, responsibilities, and system-level arrangement.
In Chirality, structural design operates through separation of concerns, modularity and encapsulation, and interface contracts.
Chirality enforces three distinct separations that each eliminate a category of coupling failure.
The instruction root is physically separated from the working root.
Agents read governing instructions from one location and write project state to another.
Instruction and working root separation keeps behavior rules stable while project execution remains filesystem-native.
Agents cannot modify their own governing instructions during execution because those instructions are in a separate write-protected location.
Deliverable folders are the project source truth and are structurally isolated from tool roots containing derived outputs.
Tool roots are designated zones for derived output such as aggregation, estimates, reconciliation, change, and schedule artifacts.
Source truth contains only human-accepted deliverable content.
K-WRITE-1 requires every agent to declare write scope and prohibits writing outside that declared zone.
Write-scope enforcement prevents derived analysis from silently contaminating the authoritative project record.
The Type 0/1/2 hierarchy separates standards definition, orchestration, and bounded task execution.
Authority flows downward from Type 0 constraints to Type 1 orchestration to Type 2 task scope.
Escalation flows upward in the Type 0/1/2 hierarchy.
No agent can exceed its authority tier or bypass a human gate.
The Type 0/1/2 separation provides a formal delegation model mirroring classical systems engineering authority hierarchy.
The production unit folder is the atomic unit of work in the Chirality architecture.
Each production unit folder carries identity, lifecycle state, dependency registers, references, working memory, and production documents.
Production unit folder encapsulation is consistent with information-hiding principles applied to system decomposition.
K-HIER-1 mandates a flat package-to-deliverable hierarchy with no nesting.
K-WRITE-1 restricts deliverable-local agents to writing only within their assigned folder.
The WORKING_ITEMS invariant prohibits cross-deliverable scanning or editing by default.
A fault in a deliverable-local agent is structurally confined to that deliverable's folder unless an explicit cross-deliverable operation occurs.
Cross-deliverable operations are explicit, opt-in, and write to isolated tool roots instead of deliverable folders.
Integration operations are auditable as distinct project-record events rather than conflated with production work.
The structural design serves the ontology pillar because folder structure is project structure and file contents are project state.
Chirality's ontological model is directly inspectable by humans, agents, and tools without a translation layer.
Interfaces between agents are defined by identity, dependency, coordination, and brief contracts.
The identity contract in _CONTEXT.md declares what a deliverable is, who owns it, and what it traces to.
The dependency contract in Dependencies.csv provides machine-readable typed edges between deliverables.
The coordination contract in _COORDINATION.md provides project-level choreography semantics.
INIT-TASK briefs serve as structured input for Type 2 agents with validated enumerations.
Every agent interface is machine-checkable and carries explicit preconditions and postconditions.
The dependency contract defines a 29-column schema with fully enumerated type domains.
Ambiguous interfaces are treated as a primary integration-failure source in safety-critical systems design.
Type 2 agents receive structured inputs with validated enumerations rather than free-text instructions.
The brief contract is a formal input specification, not merely a communication convenience.
Configuration management establishes and maintains integrity and traceability of configuration items throughout the system lifecycle.
In Chirality, configuration management is the foundational architectural mechanism rather than an add-on governance layer.
Git-tracked plain files are Chirality's sole state representation.
Baseline establishment, change control, status accounting, and audit are natively provided by version control.
A decision or state change not recorded in a versioned file does not exist for purposes of reliance.
Version control provides meaningful diffs, reproducibility, rollback, and audits independent of vendor systems or transient chat context.
All project state lives in git-tracked files and no external database is used.
Each state change produces a reviewable diff.
Each baseline is addressable by a git SHA.
Rollback is native through standard git operations.
The audit trail requires no special tooling.
Using files as the state representation eliminates synchronization burden between filesystem state and a separate database.
The git commit log is an append-only record of state transitions.
Historical project state can be reconstructed by replaying commits to any point in history.
K-AUTH-2 binds approvals to a specific git SHA and voids approval after content changes.
K-VAL-1 marks a deliverable dirty when any governed input changes since its last approved SHA.
Content-addressed approval is a formal baseline control mechanism.
An approved deliverable is frozen at a specific commit.
Any later content modification invalidates approval and requires re-review before reliance.
The approval relationship is mechanically verifiable rather than dependent on process discipline.
Regulated environments require traceability of approval decisions to specific artifact versions.
Content-addressed approval serves the axiology pillar by attaching professional responsibility to a specific identified artifact.
K-STALE-1 propagates upstream changes as staleness to all transitive dependent deliverables.
K-STALE-2 requires human triage before stale items can be considered current.
Chirality implements transitive change impact analysis as a first-class architectural function.
When a deliverable changes, all downstream dependents identified through Dependencies.csv are marked stale.
Human triage resolves stale items as no impact, needs rework, or needs review.
Staleness propagation prevents outdated assumptions from silently moving through a dependency chain.
The system reserves upstream-change impact classification for qualified human judgment.
K-SNAP-1 requires task-agent outputs to tool roots to be immutable snapshots.
Pointer files such as _LATEST.md may be overwritten, but snapshot folders must not be overwritten.
Every analysis run produces a timestamped folder that is never subsequently modified.
Pointer files provide convenient access to the most recent run without overwriting history.
The append-only snapshot pattern preserves the progression of analysis across successive runs.
Immutable snapshots enable retrospective audit of how conclusions evolved.
Immutable snapshots make reruns safe because an agent cannot overwrite a previous run.
Verification checks whether the system was built correctly relative to specifications.
Validation checks whether the correct system was built relative to stakeholder needs.
Chirality implements verification and validation through a V-model, stage-gate reviews, coverage analysis, and traceability.
Chirality implements a classic V-model with decomposition down the left side and integration with verification up the right side.
AGENT_DECOMP_BASE.md defines a seven-gate protocol that maps directly onto the V-model.
The decomposition left leg drives requirements downward from source corpus to testable production units.
Phase 1 Intake captures source material and verifies whether it reflects the source.
Phase 2 Normalize converts source material to atomic units and vocabulary and verifies unit classifications.
Phase 3 Objectives derives success criteria and verifies whether objectives represent success.
Phase 4 Partitions creates flat groupings with no overlap and no gaps.
Phase 5 Production Units operationalizes partitions and verifies granularity and types.
The integration and verification right leg drives evidence upward toward a validated publishable decomposition.
Phase 6 Coverage proves completeness and surfaces gaps.
Phase 7 Publish finalizes the accepted decomposition basis for downstream work.
Decomposition invariants I1 through I10 are maintained throughout all phases.
Phase 6 produces machine-checkable coverage and telemetry metrics.
The decomposition protocol enforces bidirectional traceability from production units back to source documents and forward from source requirements to production units.
Bidirectional traceability is the formal basis for the Requirements Traceability Matrix.
AGENT_REVIEW.md implements a formal five-gate review process for lifecycle state transitions.
Gate 1 checks lifecycle state and context validity, with agent validation and human scope confirmation.
Gate 2 generates checklists from specification, decomposition, and dependencies, with human completeness confirmation.
Gate 3 captures findings iteratively from humans with agent evidence recording.
Gate 4 reviews dispositions and routes PROPOSAL transitions to human decision.
Gate 5 decides lifecycle transition, with agent recommendation and human approval.
The IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING transition requires all CRITICAL findings to have non-TBD human dispositions.
The CHECKING to ISSUED transition requires all CRITICAL findings resolved and all MAJOR findings resolved or formally deferred with rationale.
Stage-gate structure partitions consequential decisions into sequential evidence-evaluation checkpoints.
No Chirality review gate can be bypassed.
K-AUTH-1 reserves Gate 5 transition decisions to humans.
The praxiology pillar enforces stage-gate review as a structural property.
Chirality uses decomposition coverage, dependency coverage, and review coverage as complementary verification forms.
Decomposition coverage verifies every in-scope atomic unit maps to exactly one partition and at least one production unit.
Decomposition coverage records gaps as open issues with stable identifiers.
Decomposition coverage is reported as a machine-checkable metric across the decomposition ledger.
Dependency coverage verifies every active dependency row has evidence fields or an explicit location-TBD marker.
Floating nodes and deliverables without an IMPLEMENTS_NODE anchor row generate structured warnings.
Dependency coverage serves K-PROV-1 by making each dependency claim traceable to a source.
Review coverage verifies that the review checklist addresses acceptance criteria, objectives, cross-document consistency, dependency satisfaction, and TBD inventory.
Review checklist items carry stable identifiers from AP, AC, OC, XD, DS, or TB namespaces.
Decomposition coverage addresses structural completeness.
Dependency coverage addresses evidential grounding.
Review coverage addresses acceptance-criterion satisfaction.
The three coverage forms implement multi-axis verification in which one satisfied measure cannot compensate for deficient others.
Traceability flows through scope traceability, requirement traceability, and provenance traceability.
Scope traceability in _CONTEXT.md links each deliverable to SOW-IDs, OBJ-IDs, and the decomposition document.
IMPLEMENTS_NODE rows connect each deliverable to exactly one parent package or WBS node.
TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT rows connect deliverables to requirements, objectives, and scope items.
ANCHOR rows form the machine-checkable backbone of the Requirements Traceability Matrix.
K-PROV-1 requires every extracted dependency row to cite EvidenceFile plus SourceRef or an explicit location-TBD marker.
Every non-trivial claim in production documents requires a source citation or explicit epistemic label.
Provenance traceability extends traceability from deliverable-to-requirement structure to claim-to-source epistemology.
The Decomposition Ledger serves as the system-level Requirements Traceability Matrix.
The Decomposition Ledger maps every atomic unit through partitions to production units with objective linkage.
The traceability architecture implements the epistemic pillar's provenance mandate.
For agent-based systems, safety engineering prevents conditions causing erroneous, unsanctioned, or unauditable agent action.
Chirality safety relies on fault containment zones, failure mode visibility, and context sealing invariants.
The write scope architecture creates fault containment zones with precisely bounded failure impact.
The deliverable-local containment zone limits WORKING_ITEMS, TASK, DELIVERABLE_TASK, and related TASK skills to one production unit folder.
The tool-root containment zone limits ORCHESTRATOR, AGGREGATION, AUDIT agents, SCHEDULING, and similar agents to one tool root.
The repository containment zone is approval-gated through CHANGE and requires explicit human approval for each action.
Read-only agents have zero write impact.
A failure within a containment zone cannot propagate across zones without crossing an independently enforced boundary.
K-WRITE-1 enforces the boundary between tool-root outputs and source truth.
CHANGE is the sole path from derived analysis output to committed repository state.
Every CHANGE action requires an explicit APPROVE or APPROVE_DESTRUCTIVE human approval token.
A Type 2 agent cannot corrupt source truth because Type 2 agents have no write path to source truth.
Chirality makes failures explicit rather than attempting to prevent or hide them in recovery logic.
A system that fails visibly and detectably is safer than a system that attempts silent recovery.
Missing data is marked TBD and surfaced as an open issue under K-INVENT-1.
Conflicting sources produce a Conflict Table and require human ruling under K-CONFLICT-1.
Invalid inputs produce a FAILED_INPUTS halt rather than guessed execution.
Unresolvable dependency targets preserve the raw reference with TargetType=UNKNOWN.
Missing decomposition produces a MISSING_DECOMPOSITION warning and skips validation.
Lifecycle state violations produce warnings rather than automatic blocking because the human decides.
Failures are visible findings rather than hidden recovery attempts.
Every form of uncertainty is labeled FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
Agents encountering missing data mark the gap and surface it instead of default-filling or inferring.
FAILED_INPUTS causes Type 2 agents to halt and report validation failures before outputs can propagate.
K-SEAL-1 and K-GHOST-1 bound what a Type 2 agent can see and when it may run.
K-SEAL-1 prohibits Type 2 agent execution before context is sealed and gate-approved by a human.
Context sealing requires all inputs to be explicitly declared through _REFERENCES.md and deliverable folder contents.
A human must confirm sealed context before Type 2 execution begins.
Context sealing prevents agents from operating on incomplete or evolving input sets.
K-GHOST-1 limits Type 2 agent context to folder contents and declared references.
Ghost inputs are execution-time information sources not declared in the sealed context.
Agents may not consult undeclared prior context, informal communications, or sources not listed in _REFERENCES.md.
K-SEAL-1 and K-GHOST-1 implement a defined, bounded, and approved execution context boundary.
Chirality requirements engineering is instantiated as decomposition protocol, traceability matrix, and acceptance criteria allocation.
AGENT_DECOMP_BASE.md implements requirements decomposition through four progressive refinement levels.
The source corpus provides raw requirements input.
Atomic units are normalized, testable statements resulting from decomposition.
Partitions are flat groupings with no overlap and no gaps.
Production units are bounded work items with typed artifacts.
Each decomposition level corresponds to a requirements abstraction level.
I4 mandates every in-scope atomic unit map to exactly one partition.
I7 mandates best-effort mapping of every in-scope atomic unit to at least one production unit.
The Decomposition Ledger provides the machine-checkable allocation record from atomic unit through partition to production unit with objective linkage.
Requirements are systematically derived from and traceable to requirements at the level above.
Requirements decomposition must be complete with no requirements lost.
Requirements decomposition must be consistent with no conflicting requirements.
Chirality implements a three-layer Requirements Traceability Matrix for bidirectional traceability from source requirements to delivered artifacts.
RTM Layer 1 maps atomic units to partitions, production units, and objectives in the Decomposition Ledger.
RTM Layer 1 covers the full requirements hierarchy from source requirement to production unit.
RTM Layer 2 uses ANCHOR rows to connect production units to WBS structure and formal requirements.
RTM Layer 3 uses _CONTEXT.md Scope Traceability to provide deliverable-local, human-readable traceability.
The three RTM layers provide complete, consistent, and abstraction-appropriate traceability.
_CONTEXT.md includes explicit pass/fail acceptance criteria derived from decomposition metadata.
PREPARATION creates acceptance criteria from decomposition metadata rather than independent authorship.
Review Gate 2 verifies acceptance criteria through checklist generation and human completeness confirmation.
Review Gate 5 treats criterion satisfaction as a precondition for CHECKING to ISSUED transition.
Acceptance criteria allocation traces requirements downward and verifies them upward, completing the V-model relationship.
Chirality project execution instantiates a closed-loop feedback control system across sessions.
The control system has defined control variables, set points, sensors, and actuators.
The Chirality control loop spans plant setup, content production, dependency sensing, reconciliation, baseline commit, and orchestration feedback.
ORCHESTRATOR initializes the plant state and closes the loop through periodic scans.
WORKING_ITEMS is the primary actuator that advances deliverables toward set points by producing content.
TASK+dependency-extract reruns after content changes function as sensors that update dependency state.
RECONCILIATION functions as the comparator by surfacing deviations between actual and expected dependency states.
CHANGE commits accepted states to baseline and makes the output permanent.
ORCHESTRATOR scan reports the new baseline state as feedback to the next iteration.
Chirality manages lifecycle state, dependency closure, decomposition fidelity, work availability, and artifact completeness as primary control variables.
Lifecycle state has ISSUED as its set point, _STATUS.md as its sensor, and REVIEW gate as its actuator.
Dependency closure has all active dependencies satisfied as its set point, Dependencies.csv as its sensor, and RECONCILIATION as its actuator.
Decomposition fidelity has zero unassigned atomic units as its set point, Decomposition Ledger as its sensor, and human correction as its actuator.
Work availability has no blocked deliverables as its set point, blocker analysis as its sensor, and tier sequencing as its actuator.
Artifact completeness has all anticipated artifacts present as its set point, folder scan as its sensor, and WORKING_ITEMS as its actuator.
A project is complete when all deliverables are issued, all dependencies are satisfied, all requirements are allocated, no deliverables are blocked, and all artifacts are present.
Control system integrity depends on accurate file-based sensor records.
Configuration management and epistemic controls are prerequisites for control system integrity.
Within a session, WORKING_ITEMS operates open-loop within one deliverable without cross-deliverable feedback.
Open-loop production prevents agents from making decisions based on other deliverables during focused work.
Across sessions, NEXT_INSTANCE_STATE.md carries state between sessions.
After content changes, TASK+dependency-extract reruns update the dependency graph with current evidence.
RECONCILIATION detects integration defects by comparing dependency graph state against expected satisfaction states.
ORCHESTRATOR scans compute work availability for the next tier.
Closed-loop feedback is confined to session boundaries.
Deferring feedback to session boundaries keeps scope and authority evaluation at an appropriate decision point.
Human authority is the halting condition for the ORCHESTRATOR control loop.
Every control-loop iteration requires human confirmation at gates.
The system cannot autonomously advance tiers, approve deliverables, or resolve conflicts.
Human gates function as comparator authority in the control loop.
Human-in-the-loop control positions the human controller to observe, evaluate, and intervene at every control cycle.
The halting condition prevents unbounded autonomous execution regardless of context.
Formal methods specify, develop, and verify systems through formal specification languages, type systems, invariant calculi, and state machines.
Chirality instantiates formal methods at the level of natural-language specifications.
Chirality contains invariants, preconditions, postconditions, type systems, and state machines in structural form.
Chirality defines three layers of formally stated invariants with different scopes and enforcement points.
I1-I10 govern structural constraints on the decomposition process.
I1-I10 include flat partitions, no gaps, stable IDs, one partition per atomic unit, deterministic coupling, vocabulary discipline, and production-unit coverage.
Decomposition agents enforce I1-I10 during execution and AUDIT_DECOMP verifies them after execution.
R1-R9 govern behavioral constraints on all agents.

R1-R9 include human decision rights, straight-through execution, write quarantine, immutable snapshots, mandatory provenance, no invention, conflict surfacing, brief-driven execution, and hygienic publication.
R1-R9 are embedded in every agent's instruction logic rather than checked only by a separate audit mechanism.

K-* invariants cover the full scope of system behavior across hierarchy, authority, sealing, dependencies, status, staleness, gates, merge, provenance, invention, conflicts, write scope, and snapshots.
K-* invariant identifiers are stable and never reused.
Retired K-* invariants are preserved in the catalog with retirement rationale.
The three invariant layers implement defense-in-depth specification.
Decomposition invariants govern requirements-model structure.
Workflow design requirements govern agent behavioral properties.
System-wide invariants govern global filesystem-as-state-machine properties.
No single invariant violation can compromise all three invariant layers simultaneously.
ORCHESTRATOR functions are specified with explicit preconditions and postconditions.
ORCHESTRATOR Initialize requires a decomposition document and produces _COORDINATION.md with recorded coordination representation.
ORCHESTRATOR Scaffold requires Function 1 completion and tool roots, and produces initialized deliverables plus semantic artifacts.
ORCHESTRATOR Scan and Report requires deliverable _STATUS.md files and produces state reports and blocker computation when enabled.
ORCHESTRATOR Estimating requires BOE, INDEX.md, and price sources and produces estimation snapshots per tier.
ORCHESTRATOR Control Loop requires Function 1 completion and produces handoff artifacts with a clear ownership boundary.
Type 2 agents validate preconditions at the start of execution.
Invalid Type 2 inputs produce FAILED_INPUTS halts.
Missing optional Type 2 data permits continued execution with TBD marking and structured warnings.
Design by Contract obligates agents to verify preconditions before execution and guarantee postconditions after successful completion.
Chirality defines a comprehensive type system through fully enumerated domains across four system-model areas.
The decomposition ontology defines AtomicUnit, Partition, ProductionUnit, and Objective entity types.
AtomicUnit has id, statement, status IN/OUT/TBD, and sourceRef fields.
Partition has id, name, scopeDesc, inclusions, and exclusions fields.
ProductionUnit has id, name, parentPartition, type, responsible, and artifacts fields.
Objective has id, statement, and mappedUnits fields.
The dependency type system defines the relational structure of the knowledge graph.
DependencyClass is enumerated as ANCHOR or EXECUTION.
AnchorType is enumerated as IMPLEMENTS_NODE, TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT, or NOT_APPLICABLE.
Direction is enumerated as UPSTREAM or DOWNSTREAM.
DependencyType is enumerated as PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, or OTHER.
TargetType is enumerated as DELIVERABLE, PACKAGE, WBS_NODE, REQUIREMENT, DOCUMENT, EQUIPMENT, EXTERNAL, or UNKNOWN.
Confidence is enumerated as HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.
Origin is enumerated as DECLARED or EXTRACTED.
Explicitness is enumerated as EXPLICIT or IMPLICIT.
Status is enumerated as ACTIVE or RETIRED.
SatisfactionStatus is enumerated as TBD, PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SATISFIED, WAIVED, or NOT_APPLICABLE.
The review type system defines the structure of review and findings processes.
ReviewType is enumerated as SELF_CHECK, PEER_REVIEW, IDC, or INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.
FindingSeverity is enumerated as CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, or OBSERVATION.
FindingDisposition is enumerated as ACCEPT_AS_IS, REVISE, DEFER, NOT_APPLICABLE, or WITHDRAWN.
FindingStatus is enumerated as OPEN, RESOLVED, DEFERRED, or WITHDRAWN.
The epistemic label system defines the epistemological status of every non-trivial claim.
EpistemicLabel is enumerated as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
The four epistemic labels form a complete and mutually exclusive classification of claim status.
FACT means directly observed in source text with citation.
ASSUMPTION means a reasonable inference not directly stated and requiring validation.
PROPOSAL means an agent suggestion requiring human decision.
TBD means an unknown placeholder requiring resolution.
K-INVENT-1 prohibits FACT claims without evidence.
K-CONFLICT-1 requires conflicting FACT claims to be surfaced rather than silently resolved.
The type system gives the epistemic architecture operational enforcement.
Defined types constrain agent behavior through enumeration validation, schema checking, and conditional logic in agent protocols.
An agent encountering a value outside a defined enumeration marks it UNKNOWN and records a warning.
The deliverable lifecycle is a formal state machine with defined states, authorized transitions, and transition actors.
The lifecycle state machine transitions from OPEN to INITIALIZED through PREPARATION.
The lifecycle state machine transitions from INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY through TASK+four-documents or TASK+domain-documents.
The lifecycle state machine transitions from SEMANTIC_READY to IN_PROGRESS through TASK+semantic-matrix-build.
The lifecycle state machine transitions from IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING through human action.
The lifecycle state machine transitions from CHECKING to ISSUED through REVIEW plus human approval.
The lifecycle state machine permits human re-open or archive decisions after ISSUED.
K-STATUS-1 designates _STATUS.md as the canonical lifecycle state indicator.
Lifecycle transitions are forward-only under normal operation.
Each lifecycle transition is recorded in the append-only _STATUS.md History with date, actor, and rationale.
REVIEW Gate 5 is the sole authorized path from CHECKING to ISSUED.
ISSUED state is unreachable without human action, enforcing non-delegable professional approval responsibility.
Human factors engineering allocates functions between humans and automated systems.
Chirality embeds human factors through decision authority allocation, cognitive load management, and configurable rigor scaling.
Decision authority allocation reflects the axiology pillar and is enforced by K-AUTH-1 and K-BIND-1.
Humans own scope and boundary decisions.
Humans own selection of governing codes, standards, and design basis.
Humans own hazard and risk acceptance, including residual risk statements.
Humans own conflict adjudication where professional judgment is required.
Humans own approval, issuance, signature, seal, and transmittal for reliance.
Agents may execute bounded, brief-driven actions.
Agents may perform workspace scaffolding and initialization.
Agents may perform bulk document drafting.
Agents may perform dependency extraction and register maintenance.
Agents may perform coverage analysis and reconciliation reporting.
Agents may perform estimation and scheduling as derived outputs, not authoritative determinations.
Agents may perform aggregation and collation.
Only humans author binding approval records under K-AUTH-1.
Approvals are always binding and only binding under K-BIND-1.
No agent instruction can produce an output satisfying approval invariants without human approval action.
The architecture makes it structurally impossible for an agent to exceed allocated authority.
Chirality reduces cognitive load by converting cognitive demands into structural system properties.
Epistemic transparency labels every claim as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
Epistemic transparency reduces the need to infer whether a value is evidence-grounded or inferred.
K-INVENT-1 and K-CONFLICT-1 enforce epistemic transparency.
Conflict surfacing presents contradictions in structured Conflict Table rows.
Conflict Table rows include ConflictID, Key, Contenders, ProposedAuthority, and HumanRuling=TBD.
Conflict surfacing frames human rulings as prepared binary or categorical choices rather than unstructured synthesis.
MEMORY.md and NEXT_INSTANCE_STATE.md externalize context that would otherwise be lost between sessions.
Working memory externalization organizes content by Key Decisions, Domain Context, Open Items, Proposal History, and Interface Notes.
The Vocabulary Map defines canonical terms and maps synonyms in every decomposition.
Vocabulary discipline prevents semantic drift across team members, sessions, and agent instances.
K-HIER-1 enforces a single nesting level of packages containing deliverables.
Flat hierarchy lets humans comprehend project structure without navigating a deep tree.
The cognitive architecture absorbs state-keeping, conflict detection, and vocabulary management burden.
Human cognitive resources are preserved for judgment-intensive tasks only qualified professionals can perform.
K-GATE-1 makes gates dynamic per project instance with seal transition and pipeline run approval as minimum gates.
Coordination representation can be SCHEDULE_FIRST, DECLARED, or FULL_GRAPH.
SCHEDULE_FIRST is lightweight and schedule-oriented.
DECLARED is dependency-declared with moderate rigor.
FULL_GRAPH is a complete dependency graph with maximum rigor.
Dependency tracking mode can be NOT_TRACKED, DECLARED, or FULL_GRAPH.
NOT_TRACKED mode avoids blocker computation when dependency structure is insufficiently understood.
Configurable rigor lets teams match system rigor to project requirements and maturity.
Uniform maximum rigor can impose cognitive load without benefit in early scoping work.
The eight analyzed systems engineering disciplines are connected by four cross-cutting architectural patterns.
Cross-cutting patterns provide structural logic that makes the disciplines coherent as a system.
The dependency model separates structural identity from execution coupling through a dual-graph architecture.
The tree structure is defined by ANCHOR rows in Dependencies.csv.
Exactly one IMPLEMENTS_NODE row per deliverable connects the deliverable to its parent package in the WBS hierarchy.
The tree is stable and normative because it defines what a deliverable is within project structure.
Tree changes represent scope changes requiring human authorization.
The DAG structure is defined by EXECUTION rows in Dependencies.csv.
EXECUTION rows capture information flow between deliverables through prerequisites, interfaces, handovers, constraints, and enabling relationships.
The DAG is current and operative because it defines what a deliverable needs at a given point.
The DAG evolves as dependencies become satisfied, retired, or newly identified.
The dual-graph model prevents scope drift while supporting dynamic execution planning.
Structural traceability operates on the tree.
Execution dependency analysis operates on the DAG.
Tree x DAG architecture serves ontology through stable project entities and current relationship state.
K-DEP-1 makes deliverable-local _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv authoritative for dependencies.
Chirality has no central dependency graph.
Dependency aggregation is on-demand.
Each deliverable maintains its own dependency register.
Cross-deliverable views are produced on demand by read-only agents.
Cross-deliverable views are materialized as immutable snapshots in tool roots.
On-demand aggregation eliminates synchronization burden of a centralized graph.
The dependency graph is derived from current source files rather than copied into a separate representation.
Each aggregation is a fresh derivation from current source data.
Deliverable owners maintain their own dependency registers rather than submitting changes to a central graph administrator.
Distributed dependency authority matches professional deliverable accountability.
Distributed authority with on-demand aggregation serves ontology and praxiology.
K-PROV-1, K-INVENT-1, and K-CONFLICT-1 collectively function as a safety mechanism against LLM-assisted system failure modes.
K-PROV-1 ensures every claim can be audited back to its source.
K-INVENT-1 makes gaps in evidence visible instead of replacing them with plausible approximations.
K-CONFLICT-1 ensures source disagreements reach the human decision-maker.
Chirality requires provenance for every claim instead of attempting to prevent hallucination architecturally.
Unsupported claims are structurally visible under the K-PROV-1 framework.
Chirality makes incorrect or unsupported outputs findable instead of trying to guarantee correct LLM outputs.
Evidence-first epistemology bounds propagation of false information through the project record.
Unsupported claims and write-scope violations cannot silently cross into the authoritative record.
CONTRACT.md defines four enforcement layers that check invariant subsets at specific workflow points.
Agent instructions enforce design-time invariants when instruction files are authored.
Design-time agent instruction checks cover K-GHOST-1, K-WRITE-1, K-SNAP-1, K-PROV-1, K-INVENT-1, K-CONFLICT-1, K-DEP-1, and K-DEP-2.
ORCHESTRATOR enforces runtime invariants during workspace initialization and pipeline execution.
ORCHESTRATOR runtime checks cover K-SEAL-1, K-GATE-1, and K-HIER-1.
Human review enforces gate invariants at every gate decision.
Human review checks cover K-AUTH-1, K-AUTH-2, K-BIND-1, K-STALE-2, K-MERGE-1, K-VAL-1, and K-STATUS-1.
Future tooling is assigned continuous or on-demand automated invariant checks.
Future tooling checks cover K-STALE-1, K-VAL-1, K-MERGE-1, K-AUTH-2, and K-DEP-2.
Defense-in-depth enforcement prevents a single enforcement failure from compromising system integrity.
Agent behavior invariants are enforced at design time to prevent runtime enforcement gaps.
Authority and approval invariants are enforced at human review gates.
Future tooling handles invariants requiring automated computation.
Each invariant is assigned to the earliest and most reliable available enforcement point.
Design-time enforcement is preferred because it prevents violations from arising.
Gate enforcement is preferred over post-hoc automated checking when human judgment is needed at the decision point.
The systems engineering disciplines in Chirality are coordination mechanisms, failure-containment means, and the basis for human authority.
Architecture and structural design provide the physical and logical organization for all other disciplines.
